The tree edges are numbered in discovery order: from A the search dives to B and then C, so C is reached through B rather than from A, and the edge A-C is not used. It then restarts at E for the separate pair. The card lists (A, B), (B, C), (C, D), (E, F)." width="100%"} A depth-first search goes as deep as it can along one branch before backing up to try the next. Each newly reached node is discovered along one edge from the node that found it, and those edges, in discovery order, form the DFS tree. DFS trees underlie many classic algorithms (cycle detection, topological sorting, strongly connected components, articulation points) because every non-tree edge connects a node to one of its ancestors or descendants. With `source=None` (default), the search restarts from every node not yet reached, in ID order, so the result covers the whole graph as a DFS forest. Neighbors are explored in edge insertion order, the same order `dfs()` uses. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. If `None` (default), search from every unvisited node in turn. [depth_limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Do not go deeper than this many hops from the start of each tree. If `None` (default), there is no limit. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which way to follow edges on a directed graph: `"out"` (default), `"in"`, or `"all"`. Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(parent, child)` node-ID pairs in the order the children were discovered. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist, `depth_limit=` is negative, or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Unlike BFS, DFS reaches C through B, because it follows B's branch to the end before returning to A: ::: {#3da26131 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ) label = graph.get_label_from_id [(label(p), label(c)) for p, c in graph.dfs_edges("A")] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'D')] ``` ::: ::: Without a source, the search covers every component: ::: {#95960480 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_nodes(["E", "F"]).add_edge("E", "F") [(label(p), label(c)) for p, c in graph.dfs_edges()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'D'), ('E', 'F')] ``` ::: :::
